texts: Acute severe mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture, with an occluded right coronary artery and a severe LAD lesion, needs urgent chordal-sparing mitral valve replacement with CABG.
A ruptured papillary muscle lies in infarcted tissue, so repair with neochords and a ring is unreliable, and replacement is the standard.
Keeping the remaining chordae preserves ventricular shape and function.
Grafting the LAD and the right coronary artery at the same operation improves survival.
Stenting alone, or a percutaneous edge-to-edge repair with a balloon pump, does not fix the torn support of the valve.
In the picture, Franky puts a tissue box in place of the torn mitre and keeps the harp strings, while Sanji lays cabbage on the two blocked spikes.
Memory hook: a snapped pillar: a new door, keep the strings, and cabbage on top.
